title: Officers get awards at police meeting
article: Finger gripped on his trigger, Calgary police Const. Julien Gagne had only seconds to make his choice. He chose to shoot, instantly killing a knife-wielding bandit and perhaps saving the life of a hostage.
That act earned Gagne an award of excellence Friday from the Canadian Police Association, which also handed out three other awards at its annual meeting.

Three of the awards went to officers involved in criminal shootings. They said they experienced trauma after the event but believe they did the right thing in staying calm and following their training.
Gagne was the only one involved in a fatal shooting.

"I can't even say what I was thinking during the incident because there were probably a million things running through my mind within seconds," Gagne, a 25-year-old native of St. Pierre Jolys, Man., said in an interview.
"Mostly, when you're faced with a really stressful situation, you remember what you learned in training."

Gagne, in only his second year on the force, was called last Dec. 23 to a drugstore where there were about a dozen staff members and customers -- and Arthur George Provencal, who carried with him a butcher knife and a history of armed robbery.
